headline: Architects present plans for 15 townhomes at 520 Merrimack Street, seeking early feedback.
summary: The plan calls for two buildings with seven and eight units, driveways off Merrimack Street and Cabot Street, and garages facing inside the lot, about 34 and 1/2 ft tall. Members asked for a rendering showing the buildings in context, and the architects will return with one at the next review. Also, a temporary repair to a deteriorated canal channel at 55 Kearney Square was continued to a future meeting. Approved: canal wall repairs at 145 Pawtucket Street with conditions, and sign lighting and front paint at 15-19 Merrimack Street.
decisions: Continued the hearing on the temporary channel repair at 55 Kearney Square to a future meeting.
Approved the canal wall and gatehouse repair at 145 Pawtucket Street, with conditions on materials and a mock-up area.
Approved lighting the sign and painting the front facade at 15-19 Merrimack Street, with colors to be reviewed before work starts.
Issued an order to appear for 478 Merrimack Street.
Accepted the 2027 meeting schedule as proposed.
Elected Geoffrey Harris as vice chair.
discussion: 520 Merrimack Street townhomes: Members said the ground floor on Merrimack Street should feel like a front, and asked for a rendering in context. Members also questioned the shake siding, the front-facing gables, and the gap beside the corner building.

55 Kearney Square repair: Members asked how long the temporary repair would last and whether a monitoring plan exists. The structural engineer estimated about $100,000 total construction cost, and concerns that a temporary fix could become permanent led to a request for a long-term plan from Boott Hydro Power.

145 Pawtucket Street wall: Members asked for details on materials, access, and how missing stones would be replaced. They also asked for a mock-up of the new mortar to match the historic color before work begins.

15-19 Merrimack Street paint: Members said black was too strong for the street and suggested a warm gray or charcoal on the pilasters. Members asked for photos and a site visit before deciding on paint for the back wall.
105 Market Street windows: The owner said the oversized windows are costly to replace and asked for time. The board asked for a timeline and regular updates.
